artworks.title: The Suicide of Ajax (Boulogne Amphora)
artworks.description: Exekias shows Ajax planting his sword after the arms contest — shame after Odysseus wins Achilles' armor, fixed in Archaic black-figure quiet.

artworks.title: Ajax and Odysseus Contest the Arms of Achilles
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum print: Ajax and Odysseus quarrel over the armor — the Little Iliad's judgment that drives Sophocles' madness.

artworks.title: Oinochoe with Odysseus and Ajax
artworks.description: Louvre oinochoe F 340: the two heroes of the arms dispute face each other — the contest antiquity painted as often as it told.

artworks.title: Sorrowful Ajax
artworks.description: Carstens' Neoclassical Ajax broods after losing the armor — wounded honor before the cattle slaughter and the sword.

popCulture.title: Ajax (play)
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles stages the madness after the arms contest — Ajax slaughtering cattle, then himself, as the Iliad's aftermath.

popCulture.title: Ajax the Great
popCulture.description: The Telamonian hero denied Achilles' armor remains the emblem of wounded honor at Troy.
